clue.text: Such energy gives cattle nervous disorder

parts.note: kine is an old plural meaning cows or cattle
a tic is an involuntary twitch of nervous origin

explanation.surface: A herd's jittery affliction supposedly generates a certain kind of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' is only a link joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinetic energy is the energy a body has by virtue of its motion, so 'such energy' names the type.

clue.text: What addicted racing drivers fear?

parts.note: drivers hooked on going fast dread the roadside camera that catches them, with a hint that the addicts are hooked on the drug called speed

explanation.surface: Motorists hooked on velocity have one great dread.
explanation.definitionFit: A police device for catching motorists over the limit is exactly what habitual fast drivers fear.

clue.text: Church caretaker sees service in operation

parts.note: sext is the canonical office said at the sixth hour, around noon
a machine that is in operation is switched on

explanation.surface: The verger watches a church service while it is under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sees' is a link word between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is the official who looks after a church building and its graveyard, a kind of verger.

clue.text: Cleric first held captive by haulier

indicators.note: something held captive by another is enclosed within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: in old coal-mining usage a haulier moved coal underground, so the word stands for a pit worker
1st, the ordinal abbreviation, is written IST in crosswords

explanation.surface: A churchman is the first to be taken hostage by a lorry firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'haulier' suggests a road-haulage business, but in old mining usage a haulier moved coal underground; 'first' is the crossword shorthand 1st.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister is a member of the clergy, especially in Protestant churches.

clue.text: Result of too many a mediaeval banquet?

definitions.text: Result of too many a mediaeval banquet?

parts.words: Result of too many a mediaeval banquet?
parts.note: read as a feast of the Middle Ages, then as the waistline gained from overeating in one's forties and fifties

explanation.surface: Gorging at one too many medieval feasts has a consequence.
explanation.definitionFit: The thickening of the waist that comes with years in one's forties or fifties follows from too much feasting.

clue.text: French refusal to accept a Slav as their emperor

indicators.note: one word taking in another holds it inside, so the refusal surrounds the other letters

parts.note: non is French for no
a Pole is a Slavic person from Poland

explanation.surface: The French say no to taking an Eastern European as ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as their' is a link word: the emperor belongs to the French of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French in 1804.

clue.text: Small protuberance must be cut off

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a horn is a pointed bony projection from an animal's head

explanation.surface: A little lump needs to be removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorn means clipped or sheared away, like wool removed from a sheep.

clue.text: Greek heroine makes treacle pudding

indicators.note: a pudding is a mixture, so the letters of the word before it are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A heroine of Greek myth bakes a sticky dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treacle pudding' reads as a dessert; 'pudding' is the anagram signal on TREACLE and 'makes' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra, daughter of Agamemnon, avenges her father's murder in tragedies by Sophocles and Euripides.

clue.text: Spot parliamentarian in ancestral home

indicators.note: one piece is placed in the other, so the member sits inside the house

parts.note: a pile is a large stately house, often a family seat
MP is short for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Catch sight of a politician at the family's stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a verb meaning notice; it is the noun for a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimple is a small inflamed swelling on the skin, a blemish.

clue.text: Posted to put manoeuvre into action

definitions.meaning: troops posted to a station are sent there for duty
forces or resources brought into effective use in a planned movement

explanation.surface: Stationed somewhere to carry out a planned tactical move.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers sent out and arranged for action are both stationed and set to work in battle formation.

clue.text: Gave way for the Spanish in council housing?

indicators.note: the article is placed in the middle of the other word

parts.note: council housing in Britain is let by local authorities, so it is property that is rented
el is the Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A council yielded to Spanish tenants on public housing.
explanation.walkthrough: British council houses are homes let by local government; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften and give in after resisting, so the past tense means yielded.

clue.text: Advanced about one yard? Mercy!

indicators.note: one word placed about another surrounds it

parts.note: money advanced as a loan has been lent
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise after someone moved forward about a yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mercy!' looks like a cry of astonishment, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lenity is gentleness or leniency, the quality of being merciful.

clue.text: Peanuts old PM offered to an engineer

parts.note: William Pitt, father and son, were both eighteenth-century British prime ministers
CE stands for civil engineer

explanation.surface: A former prime minister made an offer of cash to an engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offered to' is a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'peanuts' means a trifling sum of money, a meagre payment.

clue.text: What a good golfer is, on average

definitions.text: What a good golfer is, on average

parts.words: What a good golfer is, on average
parts.note: in golf, scoring over the standard is bad, yet in everyday speech the phrase means better than normal, so the clue plays the two senses off

explanation.surface: Describing a skilful golfer's typical round score.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday idiom means better than usual, praise for a fine player, though in golf it means too many strokes.

clue.text: Ogle leading batsman — a stunner

parts.note: to eye someone is to look at them, to ogle
in cricket the opener is the batsman who goes in first

explanation.surface: Gawp at the side's first batsman, a real beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the two batsmen who start an innings are the openers.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation that astonishes you is something that surprises and shocks.

clue.text: Displaced pair in need of facial adornment

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go in the other word

parts.note: to want is to need or lack

indicators.note: something displaced is moved out of place, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dislodged couple urgently need make-up for their faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Displaced' looks like a description of the couple but signals the anagram; 'of' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint daubed on the face before battle, or jokingly heavy make-up.

clue.text: Strike to switch off the printer

parts.note: to stop a machine is to switch it off
the printer is taken loosely for the sheet it works on, a page

explanation.surface: Industrial action means turning off the printing press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like a verb but is the noun for a walkout; 'to' is a link word. The setter takes 'the printer' loosely for the page it prints.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage is a halt to work by employees, an industrial walkout.

clue.text: Clan housing an Italian magistrate

indicators.note: one word housing another holds it inside

parts.note: a tribe is a clan or kin group
un is the Italian for 'a'

explanation.surface: A family group gives shelter to a judge from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribune was a Roman official chosen to protect the plebeians, a kind of magistrate.

clue.text: Ale brewed at home is anything but full-bodied

indicators.note: brewing mixes up ingredients, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: a nest is a home, as for a bird

explanation.surface: Home-brewed beer is thin and watery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges ALE into LEA; 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Leanest means thinnest, with the least flesh, the opposite of plump.

clue.text: Preferably house chaplain in ship

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside

parts.note: 'I'd sooner' means I would rather, preferably
CH is an abbreviation for chaplain

explanation.surface: It would be best to accommodate the padre on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a sailing vessel with two or more masts, rigged fore-and-aft.

clue.text: Humphrey's minister was a computer fraud

definitions.meaning: Sir Humphrey Appleby served the minister Jim in the BBC sitcom Yes Minister
someone who breaks into computer systems illicitly

explanation.surface: A civil servant's boss turned out to be a cyber-criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: Yes Minister was a 1980s British TV comedy about a minister and his scheming civil servant, Sir Humphrey.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional minister was Jim; the word also names someone who breaks into computers illegally.

clue.text: Boost for Alexander's father, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Philip II of Macedon was the father of Alexander the Great

explanation.surface: Encouragement for the father of Alexander, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillip is a stimulus or something that gives a lift, an encouragement.

clue.text: A loyal subject in Belgium

definitions.meaning: a vassal bound in feudal service to a lord
a city in eastern Belgium on the Meuse

explanation.surface: A faithful citizen living in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege man owes feudal allegiance; Liège is also a major Belgian city.

clue.text: Cowardly soldiers enter to make public denial

indicators.note: one piece enters another by going inside it

parts.note: to recant is to withdraw a statement or belief publicly
RE stands for Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Faint-hearted troops come in to retract a statement in public.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreant is an archaic word for craven or faithless.

clue.text: Quite confident to shoot if assured of success

parts.note: sure means certain, confident
to fire a gun is to shoot it

explanation.surface: A marksman is confident about firing if the hit is guaranteed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if' is a link word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Surefire means certain to work, guaranteed to succeed.

clue.text: No good leaving late service, however

indicators.note: a piece leaving a word is removed from it

parts.note: evensong is the evening service in Anglican churches

explanation.surface: A worthless departure from the evening church service, nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nevertheless or despite that.

clue.text: Poor, dear Pete did it again

indicators.note: poor in the sense of badly done, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Poor dear Pete made the same mistake once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To have repeated an action is to have done it a second time.
